Disguises

Setting descriptors with /name and Public Description, separate identities, activation cooldowns, retirement, restoration, and permanent wiping.

Opening Disguises

Open Disguises from the Character Sheet, or use /disguise or /disguises. A disguise stores a private slot label only you can see, plus a public description, biography, portrait, sound set, and optional scrambled account identifier.

Setting Your Normal Descriptor with /name

Your descriptor is the short gray public description shown to players who have not saved a private label for you. To set your normal identity's descriptor, deactivate any disguise, type /name followed by the description in the chat bar, then click your own character when the target cursor appears. For example, type /name A Weathered Human and target yourself. Replace the example words with your description; do not type angle brackets. This sets your normal descriptor, not your real character name or your examine biography. Descriptors are limited to 64 characters and cannot include color codes.

Setting a Disguise's Public Description

Each disguise has its own descriptor. Open Disguises, select the identity, edit its Public Description field, and click Save. The private slot label is only for organizing your disguises; it is not the descriptor others see. Self-targeted /name always updates your normal descriptor, even while a disguise is active; it does not replace that disguise's saved Public Description. Deactivating the disguise returns you to your normal descriptor. Changing a descriptor does not erase other players' saved private labels.

What Other Players See

Players who have not labeled your presented identity see its descriptor in gray. Players who have labeled it see their own private label plus the gray descriptor in brackets by default; they can hide descriptors for named characters in Settings. For example, your normal descriptor could be A Weathered Human and your disguise's Public Description could be A Masked Courier. While that disguise is active, an unfamiliar player sees A Masked Courier. A player who labeled the disguise Red Coat normally sees Red Coat [A Masked Courier]. Your normal descriptor is shown again when you deactivate the disguise.

Using /name on Someone Else

Type /name <label> and target another player to save a private label only your character can see for their presented identity. This does not change their public descriptor or real character name, and it does not name them for anyone else. Use /forgetname and target that player to remove only your private label. Target yourself with /name to set your normal descriptor; edit Public Description in the Disguises window to set a disguise's descriptor.

Separate Presented Identities

Your normal identity and every disguise are remembered separately. A private label someone saved for your normal identity does not carry over to a disguise, and a label saved for one disguise does not carry over to another. Each observer may label the same disguise differently. Activating or deactivating a disguise automatically restores the labels that observer previously saved for the identity you are presenting.

Identity Slots

You begin with 1 identity slot. Each False Identities rank adds 1, up to 4 total slots. Every saved identity, including a retired one, occupies a slot. Retiring does not free it; only permanently wiping it does.

Activating

An active disguise changes your presented identity, portrait, sound set, and examine biography. The base wait between disguise activations is 30 minutes. Cover Story reduces that wait by 40 or 70 percent, with a minimum wait of 5 minutes. Deactivating a disguise is immediate and restores your normal biography, portrait, and sound set.

Biography and Outfit

Each disguise has its own biography, shown when another player examines you while that disguise is active. Write only what someone could observe about that disguised identity. Edit it in the Disguises window; deactivate the disguise before editing your normal biography. Disguises do not change your equipped clothing or armor, so you remain responsible for changing your outfit.

Retiring and Restoring

Retiring an identity deactivates it and prevents activation, but keeps its saved setup. You can restore a retired identity from the Disguises window if you want to use it again.

Permanently Wiping

An Identity Broker can permanently wipe a retired identity for 100,000 credits or 25,000 Available RP XP. Wiping frees the slot and removes other characters' private-label references to that identity. This cannot be undone.

Staff Accountability

A disguise does not hide your underlying character from staff. Staff tools and server audit logs retain the real character and account identity. Player-created labels are in-character memory aids, not proof of a character's real identity in an out-of-character dispute.

Quick Answers

How do I set my descriptor with /name?

Deactivate any disguise, type /name A Weathered Human (using your own description), then click your own character when the target cursor appears. This sets your normal identity's gray public descriptor. Use up to 64 characters and no color codes.

How do I set a disguise's descriptor?

Open Disguises, select the identity, edit Public Description, and click Save. The private slot label does not set the descriptor others see.

Does /name change my active disguise's descriptor?

No. Targeting yourself with /name updates your normal identity's descriptor even while disguised. Edit the disguise's Public Description field and Save to change its descriptor.

Does changing my descriptor rename me for everyone?

No. It changes the gray public description, not your real character name, biography, or other players' private labels. Players who already labeled the identity keep their labels and see the descriptor in brackets by default.

How many disguises can I keep?

One initially, up to four total with False Identities.

Why can't I activate another disguise?

The activation cooldown may still be running. Cover Story reduces it, but it cannot go below 5 minutes.

Does retiring free the slot?

No. Restore it for reuse, or permanently wipe it at an Identity Broker to free the slot.

What does a permanent wipe remove?

The saved identity and other characters' private-label references to it. The wipe cannot be undone.

Does a saved name carry between disguises?

No. Your normal identity and every disguise are remembered separately.

Does a disguise have its own biography?

Yes. Activation shows that disguise's biography when examined, and deactivation restores your normal biography.

Can a disguise hide my identity from staff?

No. Staff tools and audit logs retain your real character and account identity.
